athen.name: Athenians
athen.history: As the cradle of Western civilization and the birthplace of democracy, Athens was famed as a center for the arts, learning and philosophy. The Athenians were also powerful warriors, particularly at sea. At its peak, Athens dominated a large part of the Hellenic world for several decades.

spart.name: Spartans
spart.history: Sparta was a prominent city-state in ancient Greece, and its dominant military power on land from circa 650 B.C. Spartan culture was obsessed with military training and excellence, with rigorous training for boys beginning at age seven. Thanks to its military might, Sparta led a coalition of Greek forces during the Greco-Persian Wars, and won over Athens in the Peloponnesian Wars, though at great cost.

pers.name: Persians
pers.history: The Persian Empire, when ruled by the Achaemenid dynasty, was one of the greatest empires of antiquity, stretching at its zenith from the Indus Valley in the east to Greece in the west. The Persians were the pioneers of empire-building of the ancient world, successfully imposing a centralized rule over various peoples with different customs, laws, religions and languages, and building a cosmopolitan army made up of contingents from each of these nations.

rome.name: Romans
rome.history: The Romans controlled one of the largest empires of the ancient world, stretching at its peak from southern Scotland to the Sahara Desert, and containing between 60 million and 80 million inhabitants, one quarter of the Earth's population at that time. Rome also remained one of the strongest nations on earth for almost 800 years. The Romans were the supreme builders of the ancient world, excelled at siege warfare and had an exquisite infantry and navy.

cart.name: Carthaginians
cart.history: Carthage, a city-state in modern-day Tunisia, was a formidable force in the western Mediterranean, eventually taking over much of North Africa and modern-day Spain in the third century B.C. The sailors of Carthage were among the fiercest contenders on the high seas, and masters of naval trade. They deployed towered War Elephants on the battlefield to fearsome effect, and had defensive walls so strong, they were never breached.

mace.name: Macedonians
mace.history: Macedonia was an ancient Greek kingdom, centered in the northeastern part of the Greek peninsula. Under the leadership of Alexander the Great, Macedonian forces and allies took over most of the world they knew, including Egypt, Persia and parts of the Indian subcontinent, allowing a diffusion of Hellenic and eastern cultures for years to come.

brit.name: Britons
brit.history: The Britons were the Celtic tribes of the British Isles. Using chariots, longswordsmen and powerful melee soldiers, they staged fearsome revolts against Rome to protect their customs and interests. Also, they built thousands of unique structures such as hill forts, crannogs and brochs.

gaul.name: Gauls
gaul.history: The Gauls were the Celtic tribes of continental Europe. Dominated by a priestly class of Druids, they featured a sophisticated culture of advanced metalworking, agriculture, trade and even road engineering. With heavy infantry and cavalry, Gallic warriors valiantly resisted Caesar's campaign of conquest and Rome's authoritarian rule.

iber.name: Iberians
iber.history: The Iberians were a people of mysterious origins and language, with a strong tradition of horsemanship and metalworking. A relatively peaceful culture, they usually fought in other's battles only as mercenaries. However, they proved tenacious when Rome sought to take their land and freedom from them, and employed pioneering guerrilla tactics and flaming javelins as they fought back.

maur.name: Mauryas
maur.history: Founded in 322 B.C. by Chandragupta Maurya, the Mauryan Empire was the first to rule most of the Indian subcontinent, and was one of the largest and most populous empires of antiquity. Its military featured bowmen who used the long-range bamboo longbow, fierce female warriors, chariots, and thousands of armored war elephants. Its philosophers, especially the famous Acharya Chanakya, contributed to such varied fields such as economics, religion, diplomacy, warfare, and good governance. Under the rule of Ashoka the Great, the empire saw 40 years of peace, harmony, and prosperity.

kush.name: Kushites
kush.history: The Kingdom of Kush was an ancient African kingdom situated on the confluences of the Blue Nile, White Nile and River Atbara in what is now the Republic of Sudan. The Kushite era of rule in the region was established after the Bronze Age collapse of the New Kingdom of Egypt, and it was centered at Napata in its early phase. They invaded Egypt in the 8th century BC, and the Kushite emperors ruled as Pharaohs of the Twenty-fifth dynasty of Egypt for a century, until they were expelled by the Assyrians. Kushite culture was influenced heavily by the Egyptians, with Kushite pyramid building and monumental temple architecture still extent. The Kushites even worshipped many Egyptian gods, including Amun. During Classical antiquity, the Kushite imperial capital was at Meroe. In early Greek geography, the Meroitic kingdom was known as Aethiopia. The Kushite kingdom persisted until the 4th century AD, when it weakened and disintegrated due to internal rebellion, eventually succumbing to the rising power of Axum.

ptol.name: Ptolemies
ptol.history: The Ptolemaic dynasty was a Macedonian Greek royal family which ruled the Ptolemaic Empire in Egypt during the Hellenistic period. Their rule lasted for 275 years, from 305 BC to 30 BC. They were the last dynasty of ancient Egypt.

sele.name: Seleucids
sele.history: The Macedonian-Greek dynasty that ruled most of Alexander's former empire.

han.name: Han
han.history: The Han dynasty (206 BC – AD 220) was the second imperial dynasty of China, preceded by the Qin dynasty (221–207 BC) and succeeded by the Three Kingdoms period (AD 220–280). It is considered a golden age in Chinese history, and China made significant progress in arts and sciences during the Han period. The core of the Han empire was around the Wei River, and the Han capital was Chang'an, very close to the Qin capital Xianyang (both are now part of Xi'an, Shaanxi).

agoge.tooltip: Champion Hoplites +25% health, but +5% training time.
agoge.description: Spartans were housed and trained from a young age to be superlative warriors and to endure any hardship a military life can give them.

archer_attack_spread.description: Encouraging soldiers to practice archery improves their accuracy.

archery_tradition.description: The Indian, Iranian, and Kushite peoples had a tradition of fine archery and a penchant for using massed archers in battle.

architecture_kush.tooltip: Civic Structures +20% build time, +20% health, and +20% capture points.

architecture_pers.tooltip: Structures +25% health and capture points, but also +20% build time.
architecture_pers.description: The Persians built the wonderful 1677 mile-long Royal Highway from Sardis to Susa; Darius the Great and Xerxes also built the magnificent Persepolis; Cyrus the Great greatly improved Ecbatana and virtually 'rebuilt' the old Elamite capital of Susa.

arsenal_philon.description: The arsenal was mainly used as a warehouse for materials and instruments for the equipment of warships.

art_of_war.description: This famous and most important work of the Seven Military Classics teaches Han commanders everything about planning battles, maintaining armies, and defeating one's enemies.

attack_soldiers_will.tooltip: Soldiers, Siege Engines, and Ships +25% attack damage.
attack_soldiers_will.description: The will to fight is crucial to victory. Inspire your troops with higher pay.

barracks_batch_training.tooltip: Decreases batch training time of units trained in Barracks.
barracks_batch_training.description:
Decreases training time of infantry if they are trained in batches or companies. Large batches will benefit more than small batches.
In mathematical terms: The training time of one batch gets divided by `batchSize^0.1`.

cavalry_movement_speed.description: Train your horses to move faster.

civbonuses/brit_woad_warriors.tooltip: All Infantry Units +5% movement speed, and gain +1 loot taking.
civbonuses/brit_woad_warriors.description: Britons paint their bodies with Woad, which produces a blue color and gives them a fiercesome appearance in battle.

civbonuses/cart_walls.tooltip: City Walls +100% build time, +100% stone cost, and +200% health.
civbonuses/cart_walls.description: Carthaginians built their city walls in three concentric circuits. These walls were never breached. Even when the city was taken by the Romans, it was via the city's harbor, not by storming its walls.

civbonuses/celt_structures.tooltip: Structures −20% build time, −20% health, and −20% capture points.
civbonuses/celt_structures.description: Celtic structures were mostly made of wood with rubble foundations.

civbonuses/delian_league.description: Shortly after the great naval victories at Salamis and Mykale, the Greek city-states instituted the so-called Delian League in 478 BC, whose purpose was to push the Persians out of the Aegean region. The allied states contributed ships and money, while the Athenians offered their entire navy.

civbonuses/gaul_cavalry.description: The Gauls were well-known for their effective cavalry. Celtic mercenaries were in demand throughout the Mediterranean.

civbonuses/greek_structures.description: The Greeks used stone construction from early Mycenaean times.

civbonuses/han_population.description: By uniting China under one emperor, the Han Dynasty ruled over 40 million people, one of the largest empires of antiquity by population.

civbonuses/han_walls.description: The Han built massive walls made from rammed earth. These were gigantic fortifications several meters thick and stretching for kilometers.

civbonuses/mace_storehouse.description: The Macedonian economy relied greatly on their vast natural resources.

civbonuses/maur_elephants.description: India is the land of the elephants. Elephant warfare originated in India and continued for millennia. It was also the source of elephants for the eastern Mediterranean. Indian kings were able to field large numbers of war elephants.

civbonuses/maur_population.description: The Mauryan Empire encompassed dozens of formerly independent kingdoms over an area of 5 million square kilometers, with a population of close to 60 million people. The Mauryan regents held the title Emperor of Emperors and commanded a standing army of 600,000 infantry, 9000 elephants, 8000 chariots, and 30,000 cavalry, making it arguably the largest army of its time.

civbonuses/maur_walls.tooltip: City Walls −20% build time and −20% health.
civbonuses/maur_walls.description: The Mauryas built their city walls out of wood, an abundant natural resource in India.

civbonuses/pers_population.description: The Persians could and did levy a large number of infantry during wartime due to the sheer size of the Achaemenid Empire and the way in which it was set-up. In general the Persian infantry was well trained and fought with great tenacity. However while this was true the infantry were poor hand-to-hand, close combat fighters. Also, with the exception of the elite regiments, the Persian infantry was not a standing professional force.

civbonuses/ptol_structures.tooltip: Houses and Economic Structures −40% wood cost, health, and capture points as well as +50% build time.
civbonuses/ptol_structures.description: Sun-dried mud bricks were a common building material in hot and dry areas, especially where wood was scarce. Although not as strong and durable as fired bricks or natural stone and vulnerable to constant rains and heavy floods, mud bricks have the advantage they are cheap and easy to produce.

civbonuses/rome_siege.tooltip: Siege Catapults and Onagers 10% faster fire rate and +20% movement speed.
civbonuses/rome_siege.description: Soldiers were well Trained to Operate Siege Engines.

civbonuses/sele_farms.tooltip: Farms −25% wood cost and −75% build time.
civbonuses/sele_farms.description: The Seleucid empire was located in a highly fertile region with productive soils. Farms are cheaper and faster to build.

civil_engineering_01.tooltip: All structures −10% build time and −10% cost.

colonization.tooltip: Civic Structures (Civic Center, Temples, and Houses) −25% build time and resource costs.
colonization.description: Carthaginians established many trading centers as colonies and ultimately held dominion over 300 cities and towns in North Africa alone.

cost_healer.tooltip: Healers –40% training time, and the metal cost is removed.
cost_healer.description: Sacrificial rituals were quite common in ancient times, whether to satisfy the gods, calm natural disasters, or even improve harvests.

crossbow_training.description: The Han had a penchant for using massed crossbowmen in battle.

dock_efficiency.tooltip: Docks work 20% faster (Ships −20% build time; Technologies −20% research time) and are built 20% faster.
dock_efficiency.description: Employ skilled shipwrights with specialized tools to speed up ship construction.

equine_transports.tooltip: Phoenician Triremes gain the ability to train Cavalry.
equine_transports.description: Early Achaemenid rulers acted towards making Persia the first great Asian empire to rule the seas. The Great King behaved favourably towards the various sea peoples in order to secure their services, but also carried out various marine initiatives. During the reign of Darius the Great, for example, a canal was built in Egypt and a Persian navy was sent exploring the Indus river. According to Herodotus, some 300 ships in the Persian navy were retrofitted to carry horses and their riders.

exploration.description: Nobody knew better than the Carthaginians where in the ancient world they were going and going to go; their merchant traders had missions to everywhere. The Chinese were noted explorers, once sending a fleet of ships into the Indian Ocean to expand their knowledge and open up new trade routes.

fishing_boat_gather_capacity.description: Salting allows to preserve fish longer.
fishing_boat_gather_capacity.requirements_tooltip: Unlocked in Village Phase. Requires “Fishing Nets.”

fishing_boat_gather_rate.tooltip: Fishing Boats +30% fish gather rate. Unlocks “Salt Curing.”
fishing_boat_gather_rate.description: Use nets to improve the productivity of fishing boats.

garrison_heal.description: Units regain health over time while garrisoned.

gather_ahimsa.tooltip: Units +100% fruit gather rate, but −80% meat and fish gather.
gather_ahimsa.description: Ahimsa is the ancient Indian principle of nonviolence which applies to actions towards all living beings. It is a key virtue in Indian religions like Jainism, Buddhism, Hinduism, and Sikhism.

gather_animals_stockbreeding.description: Breed livestock to slaughter for meat.

gather_capacity_basket.description: Workers use baskets. Increases shuttling capacity for all resources.

gather_capacity_carts.description: Workers use horse-drawn carts. Increases shuttling capacity for all resources.

gather_capacity_wheelbarrow.description: Workers use wheelbarrows. Increases shuttling capacity for all resources.

gather_farming_chain_pump.description: Install a chain pump for improved irrigation.

gather_farming_harvester.description: The Gauls invented an harvesting machine, making it much easier to harvest grain.

gather_farming_plows.description: Equip your workers with iron plows, animal-drawn instruments to turn the sod.

gather_farming_seed_drill.description: Equip your workers with seed drills.

gather_farming_training.description: Training for workers to increase farm gathering speed.

gather_farming_training_ptol.description: Training for workers to increase farm gathering speed.

gather_farming_water_weeding.description: Remove water weeds to preserve nutrients for the rice plants.

gather_lumbering_ironaxes.description: Increases wood gathering rates for trees.

gather_lumbering_sharpaxes.description: Increases wood gathering rates for trees.

gather_lumbering_strongeraxes.description: Increases wood gathering rates for trees.

gather_mining_serfs.description: Compel serfs to help your workers quarry stone. Increases stone gathering rates.

gather_mining_servants.description: Hire servants to help quarry stone. Increases stone gathering rates.

gather_mining_shaftmining.description: Develop shaft mining. Increases metal gathering rates.

gather_mining_silvermining.description: Strike a vein of precious silver. Increases metal gathering rates.

gather_mining_slaves.description: Buy slaves to help your workers quarry stone. Increases stone gathering rates.

gather_mining_wedgemallet.description: Equip your workers with helpful tools. Increases metal gathering rates.

gather_wicker_baskets.description: Equip your foragers with wicker baskets for foraging.

gather_wicker_baskets_maur.description: Equip your foragers with wicker baskets for foraging.

heal_range.description: Increases the healing and vision range of all healers.

heal_range_2.description: Increases the healing and vision range of all healers.

heal_rate.description: Increases the healing rate of all healers.

heal_rate_2.description: Increases the healing rate of all healers.

health_females_01.description: The loom allowed the creation of finer clothing for settlers. Women of the household were taught from a young age how to weave on the loom, and subsequently spent a large share of their lives working with it.

health_regen_units.tooltip: Idle Organic units +0.5 health regeneration rate.
health_regen_units.description: Organic units will slowly regenerate health over time when idle.

hellenistic_metropolis.tooltip: Civic Centers +100% health and capture points, double default arrows.
hellenistic_metropolis.description: Beginning with Alexander, the Hellenistic monarchs founded many cities throughout their empires, where Greek culture and art blended with local customs to create the motley Hellenistic civilization.

helot_economy.tooltip: Infantry Javelineers +100% grain gather rate, but −10% ranged attack pierce damage.
helot_economy.description: Helots were the servants of Greece. Unlike slaves, helots were owned by the state, which managed economic production. Helots must give a reasonable portion of their harvest to support a warrior and his family or widow.

hoplite_tradition.tooltip: Hoplites −25% training time, −50% promotion experience, and +10% health.
hoplite_tradition.description: Hoplite soldiers constituted most of the armies of Greece.

immortals.description: The Achaemenids maintained a 10,000-strong elite corps, referred to as Athanatoi (“Immortals”) by Greek authors.

iphicratean_reforms.tooltip: Athenian Docks and Triremes can train Marines and Cretan Mercenary Archers.
iphicratean_reforms.description: Athenian gymnasium, docks and triremes can train Marines (Epibates Athenaikos).

juggernauts.tooltip: Siege Ships +50% health, +25% more projectiles, but −25% speed.

krypteia.tooltip: Champion Hoplites +10% melee attack damage, but Citizen Infantry Javelineers +30% training time.
krypteia.description: Krypteia was an Agoge rite of passage, during which soldiers learned how to camouflage themselves and gained combat experience. The Spartans declared war on the Helots annually, with no problem or guilt in murdering them. During this initiation, the youths slept during the day and roamed at night, murdering any Helot they encountered along the way.

long_walls.tooltip: Build Walls in own or neutral territory.
long_walls.description: The Long Walls of Athens were constructed under the auspices of the wily Themistocles and extended 6 km from the city to the port of Piraeus. This secured the city's sea supply routes and prevented an enemy from starving out the city during a siege.

nisean_horses.tooltip: Champion Cavalry Spearmen +20% health, but +10% training time.
nisean_horses.description: The now-extinct Nisian breed of horse was one of the largest and robust horses of ancient times. They were highly sought after by the Seleucids and Persians as both rider and mount gained heavier armor as time progressed.

ostracism.tooltip: Citizen soldiers +5% health, but Heroes −40% health.
ostracism.description: In ancient Athens, ostracism was the process by which any citizen, including political leaders, could be expelled from the city-state for 10 years.

parade_of_daphne.description: The festival at Daphne was a major event of the Seleucid Empire: tens of thousands of well-equipped troops participated in the opening procession.

pharaonic_cult.description: The Pharaohs were worshipped as living gods. Their word was sacrosanct and beyond reproach, at least among the common people. The Ptolemaic dynasts certainly took advantage of this ancient custom to the fullest, to varying degrees of success.

phase_city.description: Dummy technology for use in templates requirements, replaced by phase_city_generic or phase_city_{civ}.

phase_city_athen.tooltip: Advance to City Phase, which unlocks more entities and technologies. Civic Centers +25% territory influence radius. Structures +1 capture points regeneration rate for garrisoned units. Workers +10% metal gather rate.
phase_city_athen.description: Advances from a bustling town to a veritable metropolis, full of the wonders of modern technology. This is the Athenian city phase, where metal gathering rates are boosted because of the 'Silver Owls' bonus.

phase_city_generic.tooltip: Advance to City Phase, which unlocks more entities and technologies. Civic Centers +25% territory influence radius. Structures +1 capture points regeneration rate for garrisoned units.
phase_city_generic.description: Advances from a bustling town to a veritable metropolis, full of the wonders of modern technology.

phase_city_pers.tooltip: Advance to City Phase, which unlocks more entities and technologies. Civic Centers +25% territory influence radius. Structures +1 capture points regeneration rate for garrisoned units. Decrease batch training time of units trained in Stables.
phase_city_pers.description:
Advances from a bustling town to a veritable metropolis, full of the wonders of modern technology. This is the Persian city phase.
The 'Times of War' bonus decreases the batch training time in Stables. Large batches will benefit more than small batches.
In mathematical terms: The training time of one batch gets divided by `batchSize^0.1`.

phase_town.description: Dummy technology for use in templates requirements, replaced by phase_town_generic or phase_town_{civ}.

phase_town_athen.tooltip: Advance to Town Phase, which unlocks more entities and technologies. Civic Centers +25% territory influence radius. Structures +0.5 capture points regeneration rate for garrisoned units. Workers +10% metal gather rate.
phase_town_athen.description: Advances from a small village to a bustling town, ready to expand rapidly. This is the Athenian town phase, where metal gathering rates are boosted because of the 'Silver Owls' bonus.

phase_town_generic.tooltip: Advance to Town Phase, which unlocks more entities and technologies. Civic Centers +25% territory influence radius. Structures +0.5 capture points regeneration rate for garrisoned units.
phase_town_generic.description: Advances from a small village to a bustling town, ready to expand rapidly.

phase_town_pers.tooltip: Advance to Town Phase, which unlocks more entities and technologies. Civic Centers +25% territory influence radius. Structures +0.5 capture points regeneration rate for garrisoned units. Decrease batch training time of units trained in Stables.
phase_town_pers.description:
Advances from a small village to a bustling town, ready to expand rapidly. This is the Persian town phase.
The 'Times of War' bonus dercreases the batch training time in Stables. Large batches will benefit more than small batches.
In mathematical terms: The training time of one batch gets divided by `batchSize^0.1`.

pheidian_workshop.tooltip: Temples and Wonder −50% stone cost and build time.
pheidian_workshop.description: Pheidias was a Greek sculptor, painter and architect, who lived in the 5th century BC, and is commonly regarded as one of the greatest of all sculptors of Classical Greece: Phidias' Statue of Zeus at Olympia was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Phidias designed the statues of the goddess Athena on the Athenian Acropolis, namely the Athena Parthenos inside the Parthenon and the Athena Promachos, a colossal bronze statue of Athena which stood between it and the Propylaea, a monumental gateway that served as the entrance to the Acropolis in Athens.

pop_house_01.description: Home gardens ranged from simple fenced-in areas to large manicured and colonnaded enclosures.

pop_house_02.description: Homes tended to expand as the wealth and population of a settlement grew.

reformed_army_sele.description: The Roman-style core of the Seleucid army.

roman_reforms.tooltip: Convert Infantry to Marian Legionaries, Cavalry to Auxiliary Cavalry, unlock Onagers and Centurions, but lose access to Spear Cavalry and Italic Heavy Infantry.
roman_reforms.description: Regularize the army into a professional, organized force. The Marian reforms were a series of military reforms in the last century BC attributed to Gaius Marius involving the abolition of citzen cavalry, equipment changes, and standardization of the heavy infantry unit: the Legionary.

serapis_cult.description: The cult of Serapis was introduced during the 3rd century BC on the orders of Ptolemy I of Egypt as a means to unify the Greeks and Egyptians in his realm. The god was depicted as Greek in appearance, but with Egyptian trappings, and combined iconography from a great many cults, signifying both abundance and resurrection. A serapeion was any temple or religious precinct devoted to Serapis. The cult of Serapis was spread as a matter of deliberate policy by the Ptolemaic kings, who also built an immense serapeum in Alexandria.

ship_capture_resistance.description: Marines were a vital part of ship defense and offense.

ship_cost_time.description: Employ skilled shipwrights with specialized tools to speed up ship construction.

ship_health.description: Wooden reinforcement beams for ship hulls.

ship_movement_speed.description: Train your oarsmen and sailors to move more efficiently and speed up your ships.

ship_vision.tooltip: Ships and Boats +10% vision range; Scout Ships an additional +25% vision range. Unlocks “Exploration” for the Carthaginians and Han Chinese.
ship_vision.description: Lookouts aboard ship were important for sighting land, spotting navigational hazards, and directing fire in battle.

siege_cost_time.description: The science or craft of laying or carrying out sieges.

siege_health.tooltip: Battering Rams and Siege Towers +25% health.
siege_health.description: Cover the exterior with iron plates to protect against fire and projectiles.

siege_pack_unpack.tooltip: Siege Engines –40% pack and unpack time.
siege_pack_unpack.description: Military engineers are responsible for improvements in siege engines.

silvershields.tooltip: Upgrade Shield Bearer Champion Infantry to Silver Shields, with more health and attack damage.
silvershields.description: The Silver Shields, or Argyraspidai, were the elite heavy infantry arm of the Macedonian army.

soldier_attack_melee_01.description: Often, a soldier would carry a secondary weapon in addition to his primary weapon of choice, to be drawn when the primary weapon has failed or been broken.

soldier_attack_melee_02.description: Using iron instead of bronze gave weapons additional power.

soldier_attack_melee_03.description: By adding a small amount of carbon during the iron smelting process, a stronger material, steel, can be forged.

soldier_attack_melee_03_variant.tooltip: Soldiers +20% melee attack damage. Swordsmen get an additional +20% bonus.
soldier_attack_melee_03_variant.description: Secret steel working techniques give sword blades distinctive and beautiful markings. Not only that, but the steel's hardness is unparalleled.

soldier_attack_ranged_01.description: Improving the fletching of arrows increases their stability and speed, and thus their penetration.

soldier_attack_ranged_02.description: Projectile points made of iron enable missiles to penetrate deeper.

soldier_attack_ranged_03.description: Arrowheads with three lobes instead of two inflict larger wounds.

soldier_resistance_hack_01.description: Body armor made from quilted wool, linen, cotton, or leather.

soldier_resistance_hack_02.description: Body armor made from laminated linen.

soldier_resistance_hack_03.description: Body armor made of small metal rings linked together.

soldier_resistance_pierce_01.description: Wooden shields are heavier but much better able to resist projectiles and blows than wicker-frame shields.

soldier_resistance_pierce_02.description: Strengthen shields with a metal rim or spine.

soldier_resistance_pierce_03.description: Strengthen shields further with stronger metal alloys.

spy_counter.tooltip: Make your units 50% more expensive to bribe.
spy_counter.description: Recruit a network of informants to watch over your people.

stable_batch_training.tooltip: Decrease batch training time of units trained in Stables.
stable_batch_training.description:
Decreases training time of cavalry if they are trained in batches or squadrons. Large batches will benefit more than small batches.
In mathematical terms: The training time of one batch gets divided by `batchSize^0.1`.

subterranean_aqueducts.tooltip: Ice House +1 trickle food rate per second.
subterranean_aqueducts.description: Qanāt or Kārēz, a network of underground aqueducts connected to the yakhchal ice house.

tower_crenellations.tooltip: Sentry and Stone Towers +40% more arrows per garrisoned Soldier.
tower_crenellations.description: Crenellations on the battlements allow soldiers wider range of fire in defending a keep.

tower_health.description: Reinforce the foundations in preparation of an attack.

tower_murderholes.tooltip: Sentry and Stone Towers have 0 minimum attack range.
tower_murderholes.description: Murder holes allow hitting enemies at the foot of the tower.

tower_range.tooltip: Sentry and Stone Towers +8 attack range.
tower_range.description: Arrow shooters increase the maximum range of the fire arrows.

tower_watch.tooltip: Sentry and Stone Towers +1 default arrow count.

trade_gain_01.description: The progress in handicraft improves the trading profit.

trade_gain_02.description: The progress in handicraft improves the trading profit.

trader_health.description: Traders traveling together in caravans are less vulnerable.

traditional_army_sele.description: The Macedonian-style core of the Seleucid army.

tyrtean_paeans.description: Paeans were battle hymns that were sung by the Hoplites when they charged the enemy lines. One of the first known Paeans was composed by Tirteus, a warrior poet of Sparta, during the First Messenian War.

unit_advanced.tooltip: Advanced and Elite units +20% training time, +25% health, +0.7 capture attack strength, +20% loot, and −30% gather speed; Healers +5 healing strength and +3 healing range; Melee units +1 resistance and +20% attack damage; Ranged units −20% spread.

unit_elite.tooltip: Elite units +20% training time, +25% health, +0.8 capture attack strength, +20% loot, and −30% gather speed; Healers +5 healing strength and +3 healing range; Melee units +1 resistance and +20% attack damage; Ranged units −20% spread.

unlock_champion_cavalry.tooltip: Unlock Champion Cavalry at the Stable.
unlock_champion_cavalry.description: Guard units (Champions) are professionals who wield the best weapons and have the best training.

unlock_champion_chariots.tooltip: Unlock Champion Chariots at the Stable.
unlock_champion_chariots.description: Guard units (Champions) are professionals who wield the best weapons and have the best training.

unlock_champion_infantry.tooltip: Unlock Champions Infantry at the Barracks.
unlock_champion_infantry.description: Guard units (Champions) are professionals who wield the best weapons and have the best training.

unlock_females_house.tooltip: Unlock the ability to train women from houses.
unlock_females_house.description: A festival attended by women-only, to celebrate female fertility.

unlock_neodamodes.tooltip: Unlock the ability to train Spearman Neodamodes at the Barracks.
unlock_neodamodes.description: In ancient Sparta, the Helots who were freed by the state in reward for military service were known as Neodamodes.

unlock_shared_dropsites.description: The extension of trade leads to the permanent establishment of storekeepers and their families in foreign countries, allowing them to exploit the wealth of these countries.

unlock_shared_los.tooltip: See what your allies see, browse their summary and check their resources and population count in the top panel.
unlock_shared_los.description: By means of trading and travelling people explored beyond the boundaries of their lands and drew maps of it in order to share and memorize their discoveries.

unlock_spies.tooltip: Allows bribing the units of other players in order to share their vision.
unlock_spies.description: Merchants' first goal was trading, but they also gathered information about the countries they crossed.

upgrade_rank_advanced_mercenary.description: Hire professional mercenaries to fight in your army.

warship_arrow_attack.tooltip: Arrow Ships +10 crush attack damage and +10% attack range.
warship_arrow_attack.description: Mounting bolt shooters onto ships helped give added firepower.

warship_fireship_attack.tooltip: Fire Ships +25% health and +25% attack damage.
warship_fireship_attack.description: Pitch can be made from petroleum, coal tar, or pine tar. It can be used to help seal the hulls of boats as well as assist in igniting enemy ships.
warship_fireship_attack.requirements_tooltip: Unlocked in City Phase. Requires “Naval Construction.”

warship_health.tooltip: Arrow Ships and Ramming Ships +25% health.
warship_health.description: The hypozomata brace the structure of a ship.
warship_health.requirements_tooltip: Unlocked in City Phase. Requires “Ship Cladding.”

warship_ramming_attack.description: A bronze beak at the prow of the ship, used for ramming enemy ships.
warship_ramming_attack.requirements_tooltip: Unlocked in City Phase. Requires “Flanking Maneuvers.”

warship_ramming_speed.tooltip: Ramming Ships +25% speed and acceleration. Unlocks “Bronze Rams.”
warship_ramming_speed.description: The flanking maneuver was attempted in order to position the ship for a successful ram. To pull this off in the chaos of a sea battle, a ship's crew needed to be highly trained and well-motivated.

warship_ranged_attack.description: Flaming munitions were very useful against wooden targets such as ships.
warship_ranged_attack.requirements_tooltip: Unlocked in City Phase. Requires “Naval Ballistae.”

warship_resistance.tooltip: Warships +1 pierce and crush armor. Unlocks “Undergirding Cables” for some civilizations.
warship_resistance.description: Armor for the flanks of a warship.

warship_siege_attack.tooltip: Siege Ships +20% attack range and vision range.
warship_siege_attack.description: Mounting stronger catapults onto ships helped give added firepower.

wonder_population_cap.tooltip: Enable the “Glorious Expansion” aura: +20% maximum population limit per Wonder owned.
wonder_population_cap.description: The wonder attracts many more people to your civilization.
